In 2022 the International Labour Organization reported that Uzbekistan's cotton harvest of 2021 had been free of systemic forced labour and child labour. Soon after, the Cotton Campaign, a coalition of rights groups and brands, ended its boycott of Uzbek cotton.

Cotton has been the country's main cash crop since Russian and Soviet rule, when planners turned the oases and the Aral Sea basin over to it. The crop is still called white gold. Under Soviet rule and after independence, the state set quotas and sent students, teachers, doctors and children into the fields each autumn to pick it. The cotton scandal of the 1980s showed how deep the fraud around those quotas ran.

Reform came after Shavkat Mirziyoyev became president in 2016. The government ended state quotas, raised pay for pickers and let private clusters run farms and mills.
